packages.title: RTFO 2025 fifth provisional incomplete-data QA
facts: DfT lists the 2025 fifth provisional RTFO release on 23 July 2026.
RTFO provisional publications are revised before the final report.
Supplier data can arrive up to seven months after an obligation period ends.
Provisional fuel supply is not a final emissions inventory.
No parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: RTFO 2030 obligation percentage QA
facts: DfT states that by 2030 19.474% of fuel supplied by obligated fossil-fuel companies is required to be eligible low-carbon fuel.
The percentage is an obligation requirement, not an observed emissions reduction.
The denominator is qualifying supplied fuel under the RTFO framework.
Policy compliance and physical emissions remain distinct.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: RTFO 2025 SAF exclusion QA
facts: From the 2025 obligation year SAF is reported under the SAF Mandate rather than the RTFO series.
Avtur renewable and aviation turbine fuel development are excluded from RTFO 2025 onward.
Road and non-road mobile machinery fuel remain RTFO scope.
RTFO and SAF series must not be merged without boundary handling.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: RTFO certificate-balance revision QA
facts: DfT documents corrections to RTFC certificate-balance calculations.
Carried-over certificates affect still-in-existence balances.
Issued, revoked, redeemed and carried-over certificates are accounting states.
Certificate balances are not tonnes of emitted CO2e.
Revision history is preserved.

packages.title: RTFO HMRC cross-check QA
facts: DfT states provisional fuel-volume tables are cross-verified with HMRC data.
Cross-verification strengthens fuel-volume evidence but does not make the data final.
Fuel volume remains activity data rather than parcel emissions.
Obligation-period timing must be preserved.
No emissions factor is silently applied.

packages.title: SAF 2025 fifth provisional incomplete-data QA
facts: The fifth provisional SAF Mandate release was published 23 July 2026.
It covers January to December 2025 supply based on data available as of 8 July 2026.
DfT states the dataset is incomplete and final data are due in November 2026.
Provisional fuel supply is not final aviation emissions.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: SAF 2025 data-as-of 8 July QA
facts: The fifth provisional SAF tables use data available as of 8 July 2026.
The publication date is later than the data cut-off date.
Data cut-off and publication date must remain distinct.
Later supplier submissions can change provisional values.
No later data are backfilled without evidence.

packages.title: SAF Mandate 2 percent 2025 QA
facts: DfT states the SAF Mandate obligation starts at 2% of total UK jet-fuel demand in 2025.
The mandate rises to 10% in 2030 and 22% in 2040.
The percentage is a policy obligation, not the observed SAF share in every dataset snapshot.
Jet-fuel demand is the denominator context.
No airport or parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: SAF certificate not emissions QA
facts: SAF tables report Sustainable Aviation Fuel Certificates issued for qualifying fuel.
Certificate balances and trades are administrative accounting records.
Certificates do not directly measure aircraft CO2e emissions.
Fuel sustainability characteristics and certificate counts must remain distinct.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: SAF November-2026 final-release guard QA
facts: DfT states the complete 2025 SAF dataset will be published in November 2026.
At 25 July 2026 that final release is still future.
The fifth provisional dataset must not be labelled final.
Future release dates are not observed values.
No future values are fabricated.

packages.title: UK ETS 2026 auction-volume QA
facts: UK ETS guidance updated 10 July 2026 describes the revised 2026 auction calendar.
Just under 53 million allowances are scheduled across 25 auctions in 2026.
Auction volume is allowance supply, not verified emissions.
Auction-calendar quantities must remain separate from surrender data.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime auction addition QA
facts: The revised 2026 auction calendar adds 983,000 allowances to account for maritime inclusion.
The additional volume is spread across remaining auctions starting 12 August 2026.
Allowance supply change is a market-design action.
It is not a direct measurement of maritime emissions.
No vessel or parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: UK ETS £28 auction reserve price QA
facts: The UK ETS Auction Reserve Price increased from £22 to £28 in 2026.
The £28 value took effect for the 8 April 2026 auction.
ARP is a minimum auction bid price.
A carbon allowance price is not an emissions quantity.
No emissions are inferred from price.

packages.title: UK ETS auction price versus emissions QA
facts: UKA auction clearing prices are market prices for allowances.
A price per allowance is not tonnes emitted by a specific operator.
Auction outcomes and verified emissions are separate datasets.
Price signals cannot substitute for activity or verified-emissions data.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: UK ETS secondary-market versus emissions QA
facts: UK ETS participants can trade allowances on the secondary market.
Secondary-market transactions represent allowance ownership changes.
Trading volume does not equal physical greenhouse-gas emissions.
Registry and market records require separate interpretation from emissions reports.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport 110.4 MtCO2e QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport emitted 110.4 MtCO2e in 2024.
The figure is similar to 2023 and 10% below 2019.
It is a UK domestic-transport aggregate.
Aggregate transport emissions are not parcel measurements.
The 2024 reference year is preserved.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport 30 percent GHG share QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport accounted for 30% of total UK domestic greenhouse-gas emissions in 2024.
The percentage denominator is total domestic GHG emissions.
This share is not a parcel-level allocation factor.
Sector share and absolute MtCO2e remain distinct metrics.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: DfT NOx and PM versus GHG QA
facts: DfT reports transport shares for NOx, PM2.5 and PM10 alongside GHG statistics.
Air pollutants and greenhouse gases use different species and units.
NOx or particulate shares cannot be treated as CO2e shares.
The pollutant boundary must remain explicit.
No cross-pollutant parcel inference is allowed.

packages.title: DfT ENV table coverage differs QA
facts: DfT notes ENV tables use the most recently available source data.
Coverage periods differ between individual ENV tables.
Table names indicate the covered period.
Mixed-vintage tables must not be treated as one reference year.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: DfT ENV0701 paused-statistic QA
facts: DfT states ENV0701 was paused as an Official Statistic in Development on 16 June 2026.
A paused series must not be assumed current merely because the collection remains live.
Status metadata is preserved with the table.
Paused statistics are not silently extrapolated.
No parcel inference is made.

packages.title: Public EV chargers 1 July 2026 vintage QA
facts: DfT faster indicators include monthly public EV chargers by country and region at 1 July 2026.
The collection was updated 8 July 2026.
The reference date and publication-update date are distinct.
Charger counts are infrastructure stock, not emissions.
No parcel GHG value is inferred.

packages.title: Public EV charger scope QA
facts: DfT electric-vehicle charging statistics describe public charging provision.
Public charging infrastructure does not represent all private or workplace charging.
Infrastructure coverage must not be relabelled as total national charging stock.
Charger count does not measure electricity consumed.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: EV charger stock versus energy QA
facts: Public EV charger tables count charging devices and locations by geography and power band.
A charger count is a stock metric.
It does not measure charging sessions, kWh delivered or vehicle emissions.
Power-band classification is not energy consumption.
No emissions factor is applied.

packages.title: EV charger monthly versus quarterly QA
facts: DfT publishes monthly faster indicators and quarterly charging-infrastructure statistics.
Monthly country-and-region summaries are updated more frequently than quarterly local-authority tables.
Different vintages must not be mixed without date labels.
Frequency difference is not a quality ranking by itself.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: June-2026 first-registration faster-indicator QA
facts: DfT faster indicators include cars and light goods vehicles first registered by body and fuel type for June 2026.
First registrations are flow data.
They are not the same as licensed vehicle stock.
Registration fuel type does not directly measure lifecycle or parcel emissions.
No emissions value is inferred.
